example_summary: Analyzing scenarios under Section 47 where asset transfers do not attract Capital Gains tax liability.
source_provision:
### Statutory Summary Matrix: Transactions Not Regarded as Transfer

| Statutory Provision | Qualifying Asset / Transaction | Statutory Condition | Tax Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Section 47(i)** | Asset distributed on partition of HUF | Total or partial partition of Hindu Undivided Family (in kind) | Not regarded as a transfer; No Capital Gains tax liability |
| **Section 47(iii)** | Asset transferred under a gift, will, or trust | Transfer of capital asset under a gift or will or irrevocable trust | Not regarded as a transfer; Exempt from Capital Gains tax |
| **Section 47(x)** | Conversion of bonds/debentures into shares | Conversion of debentures or bonds of a company into shares/debentures of that company | Not regarded as a transfer; Tax liability deferred until ultimate sale |


### Core Statutory Rules & Micro-Checklists

- **Section 47(i) — Partition of Hindu Undivided Family (HUF)**
  - Covers distribution of capital assets in kind upon total or partial partition of an HUF.
  - Cost of acquisition to the member is determined under **Section 49(1)** (Cost to previous owner/HUF).

- **Section 47(iii) — Gift, Will, or Irrevocable Trust**
  - Covers any transfer of capital assets under a gift or will or an irrevocable trust.
  - **Exception**: Gift of shares under Employee Stock Option Plans (ESOPs) to employees does not enjoy this statutory exemption.

- **Section 47(x) — Conversion of Convertible Debentures/Bonds**
  - Covers conversion of convertible bonds or debentures into shares or debentures of the **same company**.
  - Cost of converted shares is determined under **Section 49(2A)** (Cost of original debentures).
  - Period of holding of converted shares includes the period of holding of original debentures under **Section 2(42A)**.


> [!IMPORTANT] Fundamental Legal Doctrine:
> Under **Section 45**, Capital Gains tax is attracted only when there is a **transfer** of a Capital Asset within the meaning of **Section 2(47)**. If a transaction falls strictly within any clause of **Section 47**, it is excluded from the definition of transfer ab initio, and no tax liability can be computed.

director.justification: The provision identifies specific transactions that are excluded from the definition of 'transfer' under Section 47, requiring a checklist approach to verify if each scenario qualifies for the exemption.
director.visual_metaphor: A 'Tax-Free Transit Gate' where specific asset movements are flagged as 'Not a Transfer' by the Section 47 sensor.

beat_plan.beat_goal: Establish the three scenarios where capital assets are moving but tax liability is questioned.
Analyze Mr. A's gift of gold under the gift exemption rule.
Examine the HUF house property distribution during partition.
Illustrate the conversion of Mr. B's debentures into shares within the same company.
Conclude that all three scenarios are excluded from 'transfer' and thus have no tax liability.
